caveats: Blocked until a local model and local classifiers exist and the kid-safety evals pass, because kids' content never goes to a cloud model or cloud speech.

A local classifier's accuracy on how 8 and 10-year-olds actually write is unproven: false alarms will annoy, misses matter more, and a home system has no human reviewer between the flag and the parent notice.

Google's supervised version for under-13s tells parents its filters are not perfect, and Common Sense Media's Youth AI Safety Institute rated that product high risk and says chatbot use at ages 6 to 12 should happen only with close parent supervision and in moderation. Chat hours give the moderation, but an alert and an evening digest are a look afterwards, not supervision, so the parent alerts and the review of flagged chats are part of the base, and whether a child may chat alone is a decision to take before building.

Whether kids admitted by pairing are refused as approvers is untested, and how a plugin sends a proactive message to the parents from inside a hook was not found in the hook docs read.
Until then a parent can run a practice quiz from their own chat (MKT-02), which is the parent using the cloud model and not the child.

edits.name: When the model is down: an honest notice, jobs that need no model, and an optional same-vendor fallback
edits.description: When the cloud model has an incident, Happy today answers with a raw error or not at all. With this, when errors go on, each parent gets one plain 'the model is down' line and later a 'back' line, and the alerts that need no model keep working: the weather watch, the stop phrase, and any fixed reminder Tony has set up as a no-model job (bin day). As an option Tony has to decide on, the vendor's lower-cost model answers that turn and the chat shows a one-line notice saying so; OpenClaw's security guidance warns against running an agent that has tools on a smaller model, so this part stays off unless he accepts that.
edits.how:
Today each person agent is generated with `model.fallbacks: []`, and the docs say an agent's primary is strict unless its model object lists fallbacks, so after the built-in retries a failure surfaces as a terminal error that keeps the provider's HTTP status. Three steps. (1) Fallback (optional; it needs Tony's decision, because OpenClaw's prompt-injection guidance says not to run tool-enabled agents on smaller model tiers): add gpt-6-luna on the same per-person provider id as the single fallback for

-main, one line in gen-family, since both models are already in that agent's modelPolicy.allow under the same key and store setting. The docs say a fallback is used for that turn only and a one-line notice is shown in direct chats. Mail and kid agents keep `fallbacks: []` as the roadmap requires. This covers model-scoped incidents and rate limits, not a vendor-wide outage. (2) Model-free jobs: the weather watch (F018) is specified as a `--command-argv` job and the stop phrase (G005) is a `before_dispatch` claim, so both work through an outage. Timed reminders (F007) and the briefs are `--message` jobs, which the docs define as model-backed agent turns, so they fail with the model; a fixed-text reminder that must not be missed, such as bin day, has to be created as a command job that prints its line. A scheduled agent turn can also carry its own `--fallbacks` list. (3) Outage notice: extend the health watch (G008) so that when the existing error-ratio alert has fired for N minutes, a host script sends each parent one fixed line and later one 'back' line by a model-free send: `openclaw message send` to the pinned family handles, or a command job with announce delivery. The catalog's usual host path, `openclaw agent --deliver`, runs an agent turn and so cannot announce a model outage. `openclaw models status --check` is not the detector: its own docs say a clean exit does not prove a request will succeed.
caveats: OpenClaw's prompt-injection guidance says not to use smaller or cheaper model tiers for agents that have tools or read outside content, and each parent's main agent does both (reminders, lists, family delivery, photos and PDFs). The fallback here is the vendor's lower-cost model, so allowing it is a decision and not a default; without it an outage means the plain notice and no answers until the usual model is back.

OpenAI's status history listed 39 incidents in September 2026 and 23 in the first ten days of October across all its products. Most do not touch the API models Happy uses, but some did, for example 'elevated error rates across API models' on 17 Sep.
An answer from the smaller model can be worse than the usual one; the fallback notice tells the parent which model answered.
No fallback to a second vendor: it would need another vendor's key and a new privacy decision, and the local route is the skipped M2, so a vendor-wide outage still means no answers until it ends.
An API key that hits its monthly cap looks like an outage until the month ends; the fixed line should say 'limit reached' when that is the cause.
If the Mac, the home internet or iMessage is what failed, nothing here helps. The dead-man alert is then the only signal and it goes to Tony.
A scheduled brief that fails is simply missed unless the job's retry settings say otherwise.
depends_on: decision: whether the vendor's lower-cost model may answer for a parent's main agent when the usual one fails, against OpenClaw's guidance not to run tool-enabled agents on smaller models (the notice and the no-model jobs do not wait on this)
